data.gender_notes: Shravan is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Shravan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'shravan', which means 'to hear'. This name is associated with the god of the same name, who is the god of the lunar month, and is believed to be the embodiment of loyalty and wisdom. It is also considered to be a name of abundance and prosperity. The name Shravan carries the meaning “God of the Lunar Month” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shravan usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the lunar month and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shravan is a name that represents the power of listening and understanding. It is believed that by hearing the teachings of the gods and the wise, one can gain knowledge and wisdom, and live a meaningful and fulfilling life.
data.etymology: Shravan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the Lunar Month.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shravan total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Shravan is a significant name in Hindu culture, especially during the lunar month of Shravan (July-August). It is believed that during this month, Shravan, the god of the lunar month, listens to and grants the wishes of his devotees. To mark this occasion, various rituals are performed, including the recitation of the Shravan Shivapurana, the chanting of mantras, and the offering of flowers and food to the deity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Shravan has deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It signifies the importance of listening and applying the teachings of the scriptures and the guru. The god Shravan embodies this quality, as he is the embodiment of wisdom and the listener of all prayers. The name Shravan also represents devotion, faith, and loyalty, as it is believed that the god listens to and grants the wishes of his devotees. Wearing the Rudraksha beads, a symbol of the god Shiva, is also an auspicious practice during this month.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shravan is the name of the lunar month in the Hindu calendar, associated with the God Shiva. It is a time of spiritual growth through self-reflection, fasting, and listening to sacred texts. The name Shravan means "one who hears" or "listens," symbolizing the importance of receiving and internalizing spiritual wisdom.

vedic_reference.note: Shravan is a name mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas. He is considered to be the god of listening and learning and is often depicted with an elephant head.

historical_references.reference: Shravan is the name of the month in the Hindu calendar which falls around July-August. It is considered an auspicious month for various rituals and ceremonies.

The name Shravan is also associated with the deity Shiva, as the month is believed to be particularly dedicated to him. Mythology mentions that during this month, the god Shiva received the Holy River Ganga in his long locks.

In general, Shravan is a time for spiritual growth, religious observances, and celebration of the monsoon season.
